newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreigners seek Polish bills as zloty forced down.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners seek Polish bills as zloty forced down.

text.p: Foreign investors, who bought small amounts of Polish treasuries over the last few weeks as yields reached a ceiling, were seeking T-bills on Thursday after a central bank intervenion pulled down the zloty.

Dealers said foreigners were searching for all types of paper but focused on 52-week T-bills after the National Bank of Poland's (NBP) dollar-buying intervention pulled down the zloty by about half a percentage point in early Thursday trade.
"Foreign interest in Polish paper picked up as the exchange rate is much better at the moment," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, T-bill dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.
At 0910 GMT the zloty was at 2.87/2.72 percent from the parity rate, down from opening at 3.21/3.13 percent and Wednesday's close at 3.24/3.21 percent.
It was at 3.1355/00 to the dollar down from opening's 3.1220/50 and at 1.8155/85 to the mark, down from 1.8100/20.
The central bank last bought dollars at 0900 GMT at 3.1355 zlotys after first intervening on Thursday at 3.1233 zlotys.
Dealers said that foreign capital inflows into Polish paper would form a strong support for the zloty and could push the local currency back into central bank intervention territory.
"Inflows into T-bills will put more upward pressure on the zloty and could set off further central bank action," said one dealer from a large Polish bank.
